why_section.title: Why Cloud Migration Matters for B2B
why_section.subtitle: Enterprise infrastructure is shifting from capital-intensive data centers to agile, consumption-based cloud platforms. The organizations that move decisively capture compounding advantages in speed, cost, and innovation capacity.
why_section.paragraph_1: On-premise infrastructure creates structural drag. Hardware refresh cycles stretch into multi-year planning, capacity provisioning is slow and lumpy, and every new product initiative is gated by physical procurement. For B2B companies competing on time-to-market, that drag shows up as missed opportunities and shrinking margins. Cloud migration services B2B engagements are no longer an IT modernization exercise — they are a competitive repositioning.
why_section.paragraph_2: The economics are clear. Gartner reports that organizations completing disciplined AWS migration or Azure migration programs typically reduce infrastructure total cost of ownership by 25 to 40 percent within 18 months, while simultaneously eliminating 70 percent of unplanned capacity-related downtime. The combination of elastic compute, managed databases, and consumption-based pricing turns infrastructure from a fixed cost into a variable cost that scales with revenue.
why_section.paragraph_3: Beyond cost, the architecture unlocks capabilities that on-premise cannot match: global multi-region failover in minutes, sub-50ms edge latency, real-time analytics over petabyte-scale data, and a developer experience powered by managed Kubernetes, serverless functions, and platform engineering. Lift and shift gets you to the cloud quickly; re-platform unlocks the full compounding return.
why_section.paragraph_4: The risk is doing it badly. Lift and shift without re-platform leaves stranded technical debt in cloud bills. Re-platform without FinOps discipline produces cloud sprawl that costs more than the data center ever did. The Barbuk approach sequences these properly: a measured migration that lands workloads safely, a deliberate re-platform that captures cloud-native value, and FinOps engineering that keeps every dollar accountable.

process.title: Our Cloud Migration Approach
process.subtitle: A six-phase methodology refined across 60+ B2B cloud migration engagements — designed to land workloads safely, capture cloud-native value, and keep cost under control.

steps.title: Discovery & Assessment
steps.text: We inventory your application estate, map dependencies, profile workload characteristics, and produce a migration readiness score per application. Cloud-agnostic by default — we recommend AWS, Azure, or GCP only after we know the workload.

steps.title: Strategy & Business Case
steps.text: We define the target architecture, choose the right migration pattern per application (rehost / re-platform / refactor / repurchase / retire), and build a 3-year TCO model with FinOps commitments baked in.

steps.title: Landing Zone & Foundations
steps.text: We stand up the cloud landing zone — multi-account topology, identity federation, network architecture, observability, and security baselines — before any workload moves. Foundations are the single biggest predictor of migration success.

steps.title: Migration Waves
steps.text: We execute the migration in waves ordered by risk and value. Each wave ends with cutover, validation, rollback rehearsal, and a hypercare period. Wave planning is the rhythm of the engagement.

steps.title: Re-Platform & Modernize
steps.text: After workloads are stable, we sequence re-platform work: containers, managed databases, event-driven patterns, and cloud-native services. Re-platform is staged to absorb the cost of change without slowing the business.

steps.title: Operate, Optimize, FinOps
steps.text: We hand over to your platform team with runbooks, on-call rotations, and a continuous FinOps loop. Cost dashboards, rightsizing cadence, and architectural review boards keep the estate healthy long after migration ends.

case_study.title: Case Study: B2B SaaS Migration to Multi-Region AWS
case_study.subtitle: How a mid-market B2B SaaS platform moved from a single-region on-premise deployment to a multi-region AWS architecture without losing a single transaction.
case_study.challenge: The platform ran on a single on-premise data center with 600ms global latency, quarterly capacity upgrades, and an annual DR drill that took 36 hours. Sales deals in EMEA and APAC stalled on performance objections, and infrastructure spend consumed 28 percent of recurring revenue.
case_study.approach: We sequenced a phased migration: first the data tier to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with cross-region replicas, then stateless services to EKS across three regions (us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1), and finally CloudFront with Lambda@Edge for global request routing. Terraform and ArgoCD drove the entire infrastructure and deployment pipeline.
case_study.before: Single-region data center, 600ms p95 global latency, 28 percent infra share of revenue, 36-hour annual DR drill.
case_study.after: Three active AWS regions with Aurora global database, 85ms p95 global latency via CloudFront, 11 percent infra share of revenue, automated cross-region failover in under 90 seconds.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Common questions B2B teams ask before starting a cloud migration engagement.

items.question: How long does a typical B2B cloud migration take?
items.answer: Most B2B cloud migration engagements run between 4 and 12 months end-to-end, depending on application count, regulatory scope, and how much re-platform work is included. A focused AWS migration or Azure migration with 20 to 40 applications typically completes in 5 to 7 months when foundations are scoped explicitly.

items.question: Lift and shift vs re-platform — which should we choose?
items.answer: It depends on the workload. Lift and shift is right for systems you plan to retire within 18 to 36 months or for workloads where a re-platform would delay a measurable business benefit. Re-platform is right for systems you intend to evolve on cloud-native patterns. Most B2B programs use both: lift and shift for 60 to 70 percent of the estate to capture cloud economics quickly, then re-platform the strategic core.

items.question: Which cloud provider should we choose — AWS, Azure, or GCP?
items.answer: The choice should follow the workload, not the marketing. AWS is the broadest hyperscaler and the strongest default for general enterprise workloads. Azure wins when your stack is Microsoft-heavy (Windows Server, SQL Server, .NET, Active Directory, Microsoft 365). GCP wins for data-and-AI-first workloads on BigQuery, GKE, and Vertex AI. We recommend running a two-day hyperscaler evaluation when the choice is genuinely contested.

items.question: What is FinOps and why is it part of cloud migration?
items.answer: FinOps is the discipline of making cloud spend visible, accountable, and continuously optimized across engineering, finance, and product. Cloud migration without FinOps almost always produces cloud sprawl — workloads that cost more on cloud than they did on-premise. We embed FinOps from the landing-zone phase: tagging, cost dashboards, committed-use discount modeling, and unit-economics metrics become part of how the platform operates.

items.question: How do you handle data migration and cutover risk?
items.answer: Every database move uses change-data-capture with a reversible cutover plan. We run a full dress rehearsal on a production-equivalent environment, validate row counts, checksums, and referential integrity, and execute cutover during a low-traffic window with a documented rollback path. For multi-terabyte databases we use AWS DMS, Azure Database Migration Service, or native backup/restore depending on the source and target.
